lines.text: FlashAttention is famous for being fast. That is the least interesting thing about it.
The interesting thing is that it is not a faster kernel. It is a different order of operations.
Attention has three steps. Multiply the queries and keys. Softmax the scores. Multiply by the values.
The slow part is the middle one. The score matrix is sequence length by sequence length.
At eight thousand tokens that is sixty-seven million numbers per head, written out to memory.
And then read straight back. That round trip is what costs the time.
FlashAttention never writes the score matrix down. It tiles it.
It computes a block of scores in fast memory, softmaxes that block, multiplies it into the output, and throws it away.
So the huge matrix never exists anywhere. Not on disk, not in video memory.
The memory traffic drops from quadratic to linear, and the flops stay exactly the same.
Same mathematics. Same answer. A completely different memory access pattern.
So the claim is that it makes attention faster. The reality is that it changes nothing about the mathematics. It only changes when the data moves.
The fastest kernels are the ones that touch memory least. It is not about attention. It is about not writing things down.
